questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: discover the single-digit base case for digit recursion
questions.stem: A bakery ledger totals digits recursively by peeling the last digit off numbers like 47. Which base case correctly ends the peeling?

options.text: If n holds a single digit, return that digit.
If n equals 47, return 11.
If n is negative, return n unchanged.
No base case is needed for digit peeling.

questions.explanation: A single digit has nothing left to peel, so returning it stops every input exactly when the number is smallest.
questions.hint: Ask what the smallest possible input looks like.

questions.learningObjective: explain why an index-carrying helper backs a simple public signature
questions.stem: An orchard survey sums crates from row i onward, but the public method takes only the orchard array. Why add a private helper carrying an index?

options.text: The helper tracks shrinking work remaining while the public signature stays simple.
The helper stores the final answer before any counting starts.
The helper removes the need for any base case.
The helper makes the recursion run faster per call.

questions.explanation: The extra parameter exposes progress toward the base, such as an advancing row, without burdening callers.
questions.hint: Ask what changes between helper calls.

questions.learningObjective: select valid shrink-plus-combine decomposition plans
questions.stem: A burrow census coach sketches four survey plans. Which plans shrink the work correctly? Select all that apply.

options.text: Score the first burrow, then add the survey of the remaining burrows.
Peel the last parcel, then add the total of the parcels before it.
Re-survey the same field unchanged and add the same total again.
Count the whole field, then add the whole field count a second time.

questions.explanation: Valid plans peel one piece off and delegate a smaller remainder; reworking the same whole never advances toward a base.
questions.hint: Ask what gets smaller in each plan.

questions.learningObjective: judge which recursive drafts terminate for every valid input
questions.stem: A night-shift baker tapes four dough timers to the oven wall and asks which ones finish for every valid input. Which timers are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Countdown with base n <= 0 that calls itself on n - 1.

questions.explanation: Correct drafts pair a reachable base with a strictly shrinking argument; growing or frozen arguments never land.
questions.hint: Check each draft for a reachable stop and shrinking input.

questions.learningObjective: state what lets two mutually calling methods terminate
questions.stem: Two marsh birds trade calls: heron(n) calls egret(n - 1), and egret(m) calls heron(m - 1). What lets the pair stop for every non-negative start?
